title: Where Are Voyager 1 and 2 Now? - NASA Science
excerpt: Both Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 have reached "interstellar space" and each continue their unique journey deeper into the cosmos.
content_html:
Mission Status

Approaching One Light-Day

On Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 2:16:07 a.m. PST, NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft will be 16.094 billion miles (25.902 billion kilometers) away from Earth — or, the distance light travels in 24 hours, also known as one light-day.  

Voyager 1 will be the first human-made object to reach this distance from Earth, adding to a long list of historic firsts for the mission. Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, are the only spacecraft to ever operate outside the heliosphere, or the protective bubble of particles and magnetic fields generated by the Sun. 

Use their cosmic odometers below to follow the progress of Voyager 1 and 2.

‘Shine Bright for Voyager’s Light-Day’

Help celebrate Voyager 1's epic milestone — NASA invites everyone in the world to create a symbolic wave of golden light encircling the planet after sunset on Tuesday, Nov. 17, by flashing a message to the spacecraft with phones, flashlights, and even entire buildings. See how to join in!

What Is a Light-Day?

The milestone Voyager 1 will reach on Wednesday, Nov. 18, is about distance, not time. And it's very, very far — more than 16 billion miles, during a journey that's taken 49+ years, from our cosmic neighborhood out to interstellar space. Learn all about it.

SUzanne dodd

Voyager project manager at JPL
